title: Deferred weight provisioning and fingerprint-led loading
content:
Summary:

This doc proposes a lightweight, conservative mechanism to reduce memory pressure and I/O latency during model load and runtime weight management. The core idea is to defer physical provisioning of weight pages (device memory or host pinned pages) until the runtime observes fingerprint-verified demand signals, while using a compact fingerprint catalogue (checksums and metadata) to decide whether to stream a full page, apply a delta (safetensors patch), or rely on a cached KV shard. The design intentionally minimizes global coordination and supports graceful fallbacks for cold start and preemption.

Motivation:

- Large sharded models and mixed-precision quantized artifacts cause expensive cold-start I/O and OOM spikes.
- Full eager mmap + warmup wastes host/GPU memory when many parameters are rarely used (e.g., adapters, seldom-hit heads).
- Existing lazy-load attempts often read entire tensors on first access, causing latency spikes and unpredictable SLOs.

Goals:

- Reduce peak resident memory and cold-start I/O while preserving low tail latency.
- Provide a deterministic, low-overhead decision path for load type: direct map vs delta apply vs KV fetch.
- Integrate with scheduler priority classes and KV cache hints so frequently used prefixes are pro-actively resident.
- Make swaps and upgrades atomic and observable for telemetry and replay.

High-level design:

1) Fingerprint catalogue: at checkpoint time we write a compact JSON/TSV of per-chunk fingerprints: chunk-id, sha256, quantization-profile, expected-device (cpu/gpu), chunk-size, canonical-offset, and compatibility tags. This catalogue is loaded into the control plane (small memory footprint).

2) Deferred Provisioner: when a request touches a chunk, the access path queries the fingerprint catalogue. The provisioner decides:
   - map: use mmap/pmem to map page(s) directly if chunk is standard-format and fits residency budgets;
   - delta-apply: if chunk has a registered safetensors-delta entry, stream small delta patch and apply in-place to a pre-allocated page;
   - kv-fallback: fetch from distributed KV cache if network-local and cache-hit predicted;
   - pump: for large cold-range loads, schedule background streaming with priority hints (see scheduling).

3) Shadow mmap + copy-on-commit: we use a shadow mmap layer for pages being migrated/updated. Writes and delta-applies occur on a writable shadow page; after checksums and lightweight integrity checks pass, we atomically update a commit pointer so that readers swap to the new mapping without a global lock. This enables hot upgrades with minimal stall.

4) Scheduler integration and hints:
   - Access counters are recorded per-chunk (approximate LRU sketch).
   - The scheduler exposes three priority bins: HOT (synchronous map), WARM (background prefetch), COLD (deferred, on-demand).
   - Canary requests (small synthetic probes) can be used during model rollout to warm HOT bin for new versions.

5) KV-cache interplay:
   - The provisioner first queries local KV index for shard membership; if present, a KV-optimistic path returns a small pre-decoded tile, avoiding full chunk load.
   - When KV returns a partial tile, we reconstruct full chunk with delta-apply if necessary.
   - Eviction decisions factor in both scheduler priority and KV residency (i.e., strongly prefer evicting chunks with high KV replication).

Data structures and protocols:

- Fingerprint entry (single line in catalogue): chunk_id | sha256 | size | quant_profile | canonical_offset | flags
- Provision request: (chunk_id, access_type, preferred_device, deadline_ms) -> provisioner response "map|delta|kv|stream" + load_token
- Commit log: short append-only per-worker file for hot-swaps: timestamp, chunk_id, old_fingerprint, new_fingerprint, action, trace_id. This log supports fast rollback after failed delta applications.

Safety and failure modes:

- Delta-apply failures: if patch CRC/hash mismatch, provisioner falls back to full stream + verify; if that fails, mark chunk as quarantined and trigger background repair job.
- Partial mmap corruption: shadow mmap ensures readers never see partially-applied pages; on repeated failure we fall back to process-level reload and surface an error.

Telemetry and metrics:

- per-chunk load latency histogram, page-fault count pre/post provisioning, delta-apply rate and success ratio, KV-hit ratio by chunk, commit-log rollbacks, memory-residency by priority bin.

Implementation notes and incremental rollout:

- Phase 1: shipping fingerprint catalogue writer and read-only provisioner that only does map and kv-fallback. Non-invasive change; default disabled via flag.
- Phase 2: enable delta-apply for safetensors small patches with shadow mmap commit. Add commit-log and minimal telemetry.
- Phase 3: scheduler hints and proactive background pump with priority bins + integration with dedicated capacity autoscaler.

Backward compatibility and storage layout:

- Catalogue format is versioned (v1, v2). Older workers without support can ignore flags and behave as before. Delta patches are optional files placed alongside safetensors shards with a predictable suffix (.delta).

Open questions / tradeoffs:

- How to bound memory overhead of the fingerprint catalogue for extremely large numbers of tiny chunks? (suggestion: hierarchical chunking and bloom index).
- Should we persist per-chunk access counters across restarts to retain warmness? (privacy and cost tradeoffs).

Notes to reviewers:

- See JIRA:SR-3421 for benchmark results comparing eager mmap vs deferred provisioning on 8B/70B models.
- Opinion: Favor conservative defaults (map for large dense blocks, delta for small, kv for parameter shards). This reduces unexpected tail-latency regressions during rollout.

Appendix: quick pseudocode for provisioner:

  provision(chunk_id, preferred_device):
    f = catalogue.lookup(chunk_id)
    if f.flags.has('always-mmap') and residency_budget.allows(f.size):
      return map_chunk(f)
    if kv.index.has(chunk_id) and kv.cheap():
      return kv_fetch(chunk_id)
    if f.delta_exists and f.delta_size < threshold:
      page = allocate_shadow_page(f.size, device)
      stream_and_apply_delta(f.delta_path, page)
      if verify(page, f.sha256): commit_shadow(page); return page
      else rollback; stream_full(f.path)
    else:
      schedule_background_stream(f)
      return blocking_stream(f.path)

End of doc.
